title: Environmental DNA (eDNA) extraction using Qiagen DNeasy 96 Blood and Tissue Kit
author: Kathleen Pitz
materials: Qiagen DNeasy 96 Blood and Tissue Kit
Qiagen Inc., November 2023 DNeasy Blood and Tissue Handbook; available online from Qiagen Inc.
Training requirements Sterile technique, pipetting skills.

Important points before starting (from the original Qiagen DNeasy 96 Blood and Tissue Kit Protocol) If using the DNeasy 96 Blood & Tissue Kit for the first time, read “Important Notes” (page 15). All centrifugation steps are carried out at room temperature (15–25°C). Optional: RNase Away may be used to digest RNA during the procedure. RNase A is not provided in the DNeasy 96 Blood & Tissue Kit (see “Copurification of RNA”, page 19).

Important points before starting (from the original Qiagen DNeasy 96 Blood and Tissue Kit Protocol) If using the DNeasy 96 Blood & Tissue Kit for the first time, read “Important Notes” (page 15). All centrifugation steps are carried out at room temperature (15–25°C). Optional: RNase Away may be used to digest RNA during the procedure. RNase A is not provided in the DNeasy 96 Blood & Tissue Kit (see “Copurification of RNA”, page 19).

steps.title: Prepare filter samples in microtubes
steps.instruction: Place each eDNA water filter into a collection microtube, roll it into a tube shape with two pairs of force‑ps, orient the filter residue toward the inner tube so the bead can pass, and keep the filter at the top of the tube. Between each filter clean and sterilize the forceps sequentially with RNase‑Away, 2 × nuclease‑free water, and ethanol. Keep the clear covers from the microtube racks for later use.

steps.title: Prepare proteinase K‑Buffer ATL solution
steps.instruction: Make a working solution of 30 µl proteinase K stock + 270 µl Buffer ATL per sample (total 300 µl). For 96 samples use 3 ml proteinase K stock and 27 ml Buffer ATL (includes a 4‑sample excess). Check Buffer ATL for precipitate; if present dissolve by incubating at 56 °C for 5 min. Vortex to mix. Move each column of tubes to a new box before uncapping to avoid cross‑contamination, then add 300 µl of the working solution to each microtube and seal immediately (do not let the solution sit >30 min).

steps.title: Add beads and ensure submersion
steps.instruction: Place a clean sterile 3 mm or 5 mm TissueLyser bead into each collection microtube (already labeled). Ensure tubes are sealed, place a clear cover over the rack, invert the rack, then centrifuge at 3000 rpm until the proteinase K‑Buffer ATL fully submerges the filter. If volume is insufficient, increase to 300 µl per tube (do not exceed).

steps.title: Bead‑beat samples
steps.instruction: Secure the rack in a bead beater, balance the plate, and run at 30 Hz for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Overnight incubation at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the sealed rack at 56 °C overnight (≈22 h). Place a weight on each cap, mix occasionally or use a rocking platform. Do not use a rotary or vertical shaker; if using a water bath, keep tubes out of the water and dry them before the next centrifugation.

steps.title: Vigorous mixing and centrifugation
steps.instruction: After incubation, place the clear cover back on the rack and shake vigorously up‑and‑down with both hands for 15 seconds. Centrifuge at 3000 rpm to collect liquid from the caps. Verify the lysate is homogeneous; if a gelatinous mass remains, add 100 µl Buffer ATL and 15 µl proteinase K, then incubate an additional 3 hours before proceeding.

steps.title: Add Buffer AL‑ethanol
steps.instruction: Remove caps and add 615 µl of premixed Buffer AL‑ethanol to each tube (for 96 samples aliquot 61.5 ml from the stock bottle, including a 4‑sample excess). A white precipitate may form; keep it and transfer it with the lysate.

steps.title: Second mixing and centrifugation
steps.instruction: Replace the clear cover, shake vigorously up‑and‑down for 15 seconds, then centrifuge at 3000 rpm. Mix the lysate and Buffer AL‑ethanol immediately and thoroughly to obtain a homogeneous solution.

steps.title: Set up DNeasy plates
steps.instruction: Place two DNeasy 96 plates on top of the provided S‑Blocks and mark each plate for later identification.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to spin columns
steps.instruction: Remove caps, then transfer a maximum of 800 µl lysate from each microtube to the corresponding well of the DNeasy 96 plate, avoiding wetting the well rims. Discard any remaining supernatant. If the volume of proteinase K‑Buffer ATL was increased earlier, still transfer no more than 800 µl.

steps.title: Bind DNA with first wash
steps.instruction: Seal the DNeasy plate with an AirPore Tape Sheet and centrifuge for 10 minutes at 4700 rpm (or until all lysate has passed). If lysate remains, repeat centrifugation for another 10 minutes.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer AW1
steps.instruction: Remove the tape, add 500 µl Buffer AW1 to each well (ensure ethanol has been added to Buffer AW1), then reseal with fresh AirPore Tape and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 4700 rpm.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer AW2
steps.instruction: Remove the tape, add 500 µl Buffer AW2 to each well (ensure ethanol has been added to Buffer AW2), then reseal with fresh AirPore Tape and centrifuge for 15 minutes at 4700 rpm. Do not seal during this spin; the heat evaporates residual ethanol.

steps.title: Dry spin columns
steps.instruction: If any liquid remains in the wells after the AW2 spin, centrifuge an additional 10 minutes at 4700 rpm.

steps.title: Elute DNA with Buffer AE
steps.instruction: Place the DNeasy plate onto a new rack of elution microtubes, add 100 µl Buffer AE to each well, seal with AirPore Tape, incubate 1 minute at room temperature (15–25 °C), then centrifuge 3 minutes at 4700 rpm to collect eluate.

steps.title: Aliquot eluate for archiving
steps.instruction: Transfer 50 µl of each eluate into a new skirted 96‑well plate (used for bead clean‑ups), seal with a heat sealer, and label the plate (plate_name archive DNA date).

steps.title: Aliquot remaining DNA for lab use
steps.instruction: Transfer the remaining eluate to a second skirted 96‑well plate, label (plate_name lab DNA date), and store for downstream applications.

steps.title: Quantify DNA with Quant‑iT kit
steps.instruction: Measure total DNA concentration using the Quant‑iT kit on a plate reader according to the kit instructions.
